result.title: Effects of Conventional, Adaptive, and AI-Powered Upscaling on the Legibility of License Plates
result.summary: Small details in digital images -- a face, a street sign, a license plate -- are routinely upscaled in hopes of making them interpretable. Upscaling options now range from conventional interpolation, whose operations are spatially invariant and fully explainable, to AI-powered methods that synthesize detail potentially absent from the source. Here, we ask which of these techniques most reliably helps human readers. In two online experiments, we measured legibility of 255 US license plates ranging in resolution from 128 to 8 pixels tall, as well as their legibility after upscaling by eight different methods. Legibility of the un-upscaled plates collapsed from ceiling to floor across a narrow band of plate heights (32 to 10 pixels). Conventional upscaling techniques (bilinear, bicubic, and Lanczos interpolation) gave modest gains of about 5-9 percentage points within this range. Nearest-neighbor interpolation, however, was harmful, rendering unreadable many plates that were readable without any upscaling. Advanced methods diverged: SwinIR, an open-source AI enhancer, raised performance by up to 38 points relative to no upscaling, while an adaptive denoiser-based image prior and commercial AI upscaler tended to impair legibility. We found no strong evidence of consistent character hallucinations across methods. Decomposing the task, conventional interpolators mainly helped readers count characters, whereas SwinIR alone made the characters themselves more identifiable.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究用两项在线实验考察 255 张不同高度（128 至 8 像素）美国车牌在八种上采样方法前后的可读性，发现传统插值仅带来约 5–9 个百分点提升、最近邻反而有害，SwinIR 最多提升 38 个百分点，而某些 AI 先验与商用上采样器却降低可读性，且未发现明显的字符幻觉。
AI.relevance_reason: 属人眼可读性研究，不涉及 latent 推理或多模态模型，但其关于上采样合成细节是提升还是污染细粒度证据、以及缺失细节是否被凭空生成的结论，可供核查视觉前端处理对 VLM 细粒度视觉证据筛选的潜在影响。
